name: Action
description: An activity that someone does on purpose: it starts and ends, can be going on right now, and you can choose to do it or refuse.

examples.en: He wants to buy a new phone.

hen.note: An activity has no degree, so it can't take 很. Use a frequency adverb, or put 很 on a state verb like 喜歡.

wrong.why: 買 is an action; 很 only grades states.

le.label: 買了
le.note: 了 right after the verb marks the action as done.

examples.zh: 我去年每天都學了中文。
examples.en: (meant: last year I studied Chinese every day)

wrong.why: 了 marks a completed event, not past time. Habits take no 了, even in the past.
An action that didn't happen can't be completed: 沒 + verb takes no 了.

zai.label: 在買
zai.note: 在 before the verb: the action is in progress right now.

examples.zh: 我打電話的時候，他在洗澡。
examples.en: When I called, he was taking a shower.

zhe.label: 坐著
zhe.note: 著 marks the lasting state an action leaves behind, or the manner of another action. In Taiwan it is rarely used for 'in progress'.

examples.en: He watches the game sitting down.
(meant: the monk thought for a while)

wrong.why: 著 is an ongoing state with no end point, so it can't take a duration. A completed stretch of time takes 了.

reduplication.label: 看看 (a little)
reduplication.note: Doubling softens the action: do it a little, briefly, casually. Two-syllable verbs double as ABAB.

examples.en: Take a look at this book.
I want to learn Chinese, please teach me.

wrong.why: AABB doubling is for state verbs (高高興興). Action verbs repeat the whole word: ABAB.

negation.label: 不 / 沒
negation.note: 不: won't, doesn't (habits, intentions, the future). 沒: didn't, hasn't (the action didn't happen).

examples.zh: 你不買票，我就不讓你進去。
examples.en: If you don't buy a ticket, I won't let you in.
I have no money on me today (I didn't bring any).

wrong.why: 沒 says that something didn't happen, so it can't refer to the future. Use 不.

name: State
description: A quality, feeling or piece of knowledge that simply holds, with no start or end in view. Most English adjectives belong here.

hen.label: 很冷
hen.note: States have a degree. With plain state verbs 很 is also the neutral link to the subject, where English uses 'is'.

wrong.why: A state verb is the predicate on its own; it doesn't take 是.

le.label: — but 天冷了 means 'it got cold'
le.note: A state isn't an action, so it can't be 'done' and 了 isn't a past tense. 了 at the end of the sentence does work, with a different meaning: the state is new, it has become so.

wrong.why: A past state needs no 了; the time word already says when. 了 would mean 'it had become cold'.

examples.en: (meant: as a child I liked ants)

wrong.why: A liking that lasted through a period in the past is a state and takes no 了.

zai.note: A state isn't an activity, so it can't be in progress. 'Right now' is said with 現在.

wrong.why: 在 + verb is for activities in progress; a state just holds.

zhe.label: some: 愛著
zhe.note: Most states already last, so they don't take 著. A few feelings take it to stress that they go on.

wrong.why: Qualities like 高 never take 著.

reduplication.label: 高高的 (intensifies)
reduplication.note: Doubling makes the description more vivid and personal, and takes 的. Two-syllable ones double as AABB. Not every state verb doubles: 貴, 近, 忙, 新, 少 don't.

examples.en: Her eyes are nice and big.

wrong.why: Doubling already intensifies, so it doesn't combine with 很.
A doubled state verb needs 的 after it.

examples.zh: 老闆，我要一杯熱熱的咖啡。

wrong.why: Doubling expresses the speaker's feeling, praise or complaint. A plain factual request like ordering uses the bare verb.

negation.label: 不
negation.note: States are negated with 不, also in the past.

examples.en: He didn't know / doesn't know about this.
(meant: as a child I didn't like vegetables)

wrong.why: 沒 negates events. A state is negated with 不, whatever the time.

name: Process
description: The instant something changes from one state into another; what matters is the result.

hen.note: A change either happened or not; it has no degree. How bad the result is goes in a 得 complement.

wrong.why: 病 'get sick' is a change, not a quality, so it can't take 很.

le.label: 死了
le.note: 了 says the change has happened; process verbs almost always appear with it.

zai.note: A change happens in an instant, so it can't be in progress. 'About to change' is 快…了.

examples.en: The flowers are dying (about to die).

wrong.why: 死 is the instant of dying, not an activity that can be in progress.

zhe.note: The state after the change is reported with 了, not 著.

wrong.why: 著 is for lasting actions and states; a change is over in an instant.

reduplication.note: An instant change can't be done 'a little', so it doesn't double.

wrong.why: Only action verbs double to mean 'a little'; 忘記 is a change.

negation.label: 沒
negation.note: A change either happened or didn't, so it's negated with 沒.

examples.zh: 中文課還沒結束，所以我不能回國。
examples.en: Chinese class isn't over yet, so I can't go home.

examples.zh: 我還沒決定要不要去旅行。
examples.en: I haven't decided yet whether to travel.

wrong.why: 不壞 is the state 'not bad'. 'Not broken' means the change didn't happen: 沒壞.
